get.description: List disputes within a date range based on certain criteria. This endpoint can be used for debugging or synchronizing the disputes from Afterpay if/when you are unable to use the webhook method.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Payment or Order token using which you can filter the list.

parameters.name: merchant
parameters.description: Merchant token using which you can filter the list.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Dispute status using which you can filter the list.

parameters.name: openedAfter
parameters.description: Filter disputes that were created on or after this timestamp (inclusive).

parameters.name: openedBefore
parameters.description: Filter disputes that were created on or before this timestamp (inclusive).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of records that you want returned from this request.

get.description: Get detailed information about a dispute.

post.description:
The Respond to the Dispute endpoint allows a merchant to submit evidence for the dispute. This is only allowed if the dispute is the state `needs_response`.

Merchants only have one opportunity to submit evidence. Once a 200 response is received, this information cannot be updated or changed.

200.description: When successful, returns the updated dispute object

id.description: A unique ID given to a dispute.

evidence.description: Evidence for the dispute. Note that there should be at least one valid field.

get.description:
Merchants can call this endpoint to accept a dispute case. The endpoint only works if the dispute is in a non-terminal state (the status is not `won` or `lost`).

> **Note:** Calling the API changes the dispute status to lost.

200.description: If successful, returns the updated dispute object.

post.description: Use this endpoint to upload files for disputes.

file.description: The file you want to upload.

fileType.description: The type of file. Only `dispute_evidence` is supported.

get.description: Use this endpoint to retrieve files for disputes.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the file to be retrieved.

200.description: Indicates that the file has been retrieved successfully.

404.description: Not Found. The corresponding entity can't be found for the merchant.

412.description: Precondition Failed. Invalid action for the dispute case, or the refund amount is larger than the refundable amount.

413.description: Request Entity Too Large. The uploaded file is too large. It must be less than 10 MB.

415.description: Unsupported Media Type. Afterpay does not support the filetype of the uploaded file. It must be: GIF, PDF, JPEG, or PNG.

422.description: Unprocessable Entity. Invalid parameter in the Dispute API request.

429.description: Too Many Requests. Too many requests in a short period of time, retry later.

DisputeStatus.description: The current state of the dispute. Values depend on how the dispute state machine is modeled.
DisputeStatus.title: DisputeStatus

DisputeClosingReason.description: A reason indicating how the final decision on the dispute was reached. Recommended possible values listed in Closing Reasons.
DisputeClosingReason.title: DisputeClosingReason

transactionAmount.description: The transaction amount for the order.

network.description: The payment network used by the customer. (For example, `Visa` or `MasterCard`)

order.description: The token of the order that the dispute is for.

status.description: The current state of the dispute. Values depend on how the dispute state machine is modeled.

open.description: `True` if a final decision on the dispute hasn't been made yet.

responseDueBy.description: Deadline by which the merchant must respond to the dispute. (Epoch timestamp in seconds, timezone UTC +0.00)

createdAt.description: A timestamp indicating when the dispute was created. (Epoch timestamp in seconds, timezone UTC +0.00)

openingNote.description: Text from the customer describing why the dispute was opened or the reason for the complaint. While dispute category codes are helpful at informing what a merchant should present, it doesn’t provide reasoning behind the customer’s complaint. In some cases, this can help merchants troubleshoot the dispute directly with their customers.

openingNoteAttachments.description: Attachments to supplement the `openingNote` if the customer provided photos or screenshots as part of their dispute description.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the dispute was updated. (Epoch timestamp in seconds, timezone UTC +0.00)

closingReason.description: A reason indicating how the final decision on the dispute was reached. Recommended possible values listed in Closing Reasons.

closingNote.description: Text describing in detail how the final decision on the dispute was reached. This supplements the `closingReason`.

merchantOrderId.description: The identifier for the transaction on the merchant side.

transactionDate.description: The timestamp of the order created by the customer. (Epoch timestamp in seconds, timezone UTC +0.00)

meta.description: The extra information for merchants to match payment.

data.description: An array of dispute objects that match the filter criteria in the request.

productDescription.description: A description of the product or service and any relevant details on how this was presented to the customer at the time of purchase.

refundPolicy.description: Token of the file upload. The merchant’s refund policy, as shown or provided to the customer.

refundPolicyDisclosure.description: An explanation of how and when the customer was shown or provided with the merchant’s refund policy prior to purchase.

refundRefusalExplanation.description: The merchant’s explanation for why the customer is not entitled to a refund.

shippingDocumentation.description: Token of the file upload. A shipping label or receipt for the disputed payment.

shippingAddress.description: The address to which a physical product was shipped.

shippingDate.description: In cases of physical products, the date that a physical product began its route to the shipping address in a clear human-readable format. This date should be prior to the date of the dispute.

shippingCarrier.description: In cases of physical products, the delivery service that shipped a physical product, such as Fedex, UPS, USPS, etc. If multiple carriers were used for this purchase, separate them with commas.

shippingTrackingNumber.description: The tracking number for a physical product, obtained from the delivery service.

uncategorizedFile.description: Token of the file upload. Additional file that’s not in any of the categories above.

uncategorizedText.description: Any additional text deemed relevant by the merchant.

id.description: The ID token of the file.

createdAt.description: The timestamp indicating when the file was uploaded.

expiresAt.description: The timestamp indicating when the uploaded file expires.

url.description: The link of the file to be retrieved.

expiresAt.description: The timestamp indicating the expiration of the link.
